title: regional-peak-token-surge-plan-2026-q3
body:
Summary:
This working-plan estimates hosted API peak tokens/sec and QPS for Q3 2026, converts demand into GPU requirements by region, and proposes headroom targets and operational levers. This is intentionally conservative: goal is to define an operationally safe fleet sizing and short-term autoscale/playbook while we finish more granular per-customer allocations.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Forecast window: Q3 2026 (focus on the next 90d of peaks).
- Request mix (by model family): 60% 7B-class, 30% 13B-class, 10% 70B-class.
- Average tokens per request at peak: 60 tokens (measured from recent production histograms).
- Regional peak QPS (expected 99th-percentile sustained 60s): NA=800 QPS, EU=300 QPS, APAC=200 QPS (total 1,300 QPS).
- Measured per-GPU sustained token throughput (seq_len ~ 1024, dynamic batching):
  - H100-80GB (reference): 7B -> 20,000 tps, 13B -> 9,000 tps, 70B -> 2,500 tps.
  - A100-80GB: 7B -> 15,000 tps, 13B -> 7,000 tps, 70B -> 2,000 tps.
  - L4 (edge/cheap): 7B -> 4,500 tps, 13B -> 2,000 tps, 70B -> 600 tps.
- Model routing is flexible (any GPU class can serve multiple model sizes, but throughput varies as above).
- Target headroom for production pools (safety margin): 40% for regional pools + 2-GPU warm spare in global warm pool for fast cross-region fallback.

Calculated demand (baseline):
- Total tokens/sec at peak = total QPS * avg tokens = 1,300 * 60 = 78,000 tokens/sec.
- By region:
  - NA: 800 QPS -> 48,000 tps (61.5% of total)
  - EU: 300 QPS -> 18,000 tps (23.1%)
  - APAC: 200 QPS -> 12,000 tps (15.4%)
- By model family (global demand):
  - 7B: 0.6 * 78,000 = 46,800 tps
  - 13B: 0.3 * 78,000 = 23,400 tps
  - 70B: 0.1 * 78,000 = 7,800 tps

GPU requirement (reference sizing using H100 throughput):
- GPUs needed per model family (round up to nearest whole GPU):
  - 7B: 46,800 / 20,000 = 2.34 -> 3 GPUs
  - 13B: 23,400 / 9,000 = 2.6 -> 3 GPUs
  - 70B: 7,800 / 2,500 = 3.12 -> 4 GPUs
- Total raw H100s required (no headroom): 3 + 3 + 4 = 10 GPUs.
- Apply 40% regional headroom multiplier: 10 * 1.4 = 14 GPUs.

Regional allocation (apply tokens/sec share to final pool of 14 GPUs):
- NA (61.5%): 14 * 0.615 = 8.6 -> 9 GPUs (primary NA pool)
- EU (23.1%): 14 * 0.231 = 3.2 -> 3 GPUs (primary EU pool)
- APAC (15.4%): 14 * 0.154 = 2.1 -> 2 GPUs (primary APAC pool)
- Global warm pool: +2 H100s (cross-region warm spares / cold-fallback reserve)
- Total fleet (H100-equivalent): 16 GPUs (14 provisioned regionally + 2 warm).

Notes on heterogenous fleet mapping: if fleet mixes A100 and L4, convert using H100-equivalent capacity by tps ratios. Example conversion to A100-equivalents (using 7B numbers for rough conversion): H100 7B=20k vs A100 7B=15k => 1 H100 ~1.33 A100. We recommend expressing procurement as "H100-equivalent units" in capacity dashboards to avoid double-counting.

Reserved capacity / enterprise commitments:
- Policy: reserve 20% of NA primary pool for Reserved/Dedicated customers during declared business hours (08:00-20:00 local). For NA primary pool of 9 GPUs, reserve 2 GPUs (round-up). That leaves 7 GPUs available for public hosted traffic in NA daytime.
- Rationale: Enterprise SLAs require predictable throughput; reserving from regional pool is cheaper than separate dedicated hardware in the short term.

Autoscaling & operational levers:
- Short-term: maintain 2 warm GPUs in global pool (H100-equivalent) that can be hot-swapped into regions in <5m using routing policy. Use container-level warm start to avoid OOM.
- Medium-term: target autoscale cooldown at 180s and max burst add of 4 GPUs per minute per region during sustained surge >95th percentile.
- Caching & batching: enable prefix KV caching for high-reuse customers and soft-rate-limit best-effort low-tier traffic during sustained overload; this reduces effective tokens/sec by up to 18% for typical conversational workloads.

Failure & fallback plan (99.9% aim):
- If regional pool saturated: route to warm pool (if available), otherwise fallback to smaller quantized variants (e.g., 13B->7B or q4 variants) according to quality policy.
- If warm pool is also saturated for >120s: apply tiered request-shedding (best-effort) with 429 response + retry-after header for low-tier customers; enterprise traffic kept via reserved slots.

Operational checklist (short-term actions):
- [ ] Instrument H100-equivalent dashboard (tokens/sec, GPUs provisioned, hot-warm-cold counts) by 2026-06-01 (owner: Daniel Kim).
- [ ] Implement headroom multiplier knob in autoscaler configs (owner: María Lopez).
- [ ] Create routing policy for NA->warm pool failover with 5m cold-start SLA (owner: Ethan Zhao).
- [ ] Run a controlled regional failover test by 2026-06-20 (owner: eng-sre).

Open questions / risks:
- Throughput variability by model implementation (kernel selection) can swing effective tps per GPU +/-20% for some versions. We need continuous benchmarking per model version and sequence length distribution.
- APAC cloud-region GPU procurement lead times may be >8 weeks; consider rebalancing warm spares in NA/EU to act as contingency.
- Enterprise commitments may grow and require converting warm reserve to dedicated capacity; monitor usage and alert when committed usage >60% of reserved slots.

Appendix: quick example calculation (NA baseline, H100-only):
- NA demand 48,000 tps. Using H100-equivalents and the model mix above, raw GPUs = 48,000 / (weighted tps per GPU). Weighted tps per GPU = (0.6*20k + 0.3*9k + 0.1*2.5k) = 12,000 + 2,700 + 250 = 14,950 tps/GPU. Raw GPUs = 48,000/14,950 = 3.21 -> round up to 4; with 40% headroom -> 4 * 1.4 = 5.6 -> round up to 6 GPUs for NA primary (note: regional rounding and global pooling lead to slightly different allocation above; both methods shown to surface rounding choices).

Decision request (for short-term exec sign-off):
- Approve H100-equivalent operational fleet target of 16 GPUs (14 regional provisioned + 2 warm) for Q3 baseline with 40% headroom and 20% NA reservation for enterprise. This allows expected 99th-percentile coverage for the forecasted peak with operational safety margin.

Change log:
- 2026-05-04: initial draft (Asha Patel).
- 2026-05-21: updated regional QPS after sales input (María Lopez).
- 2026-06-12: added autoscale knobs + warm pool definitions (Daniel Kim).

Comments / next steps: add per-customer weighting and perform a heatmap sensitivity run (±20% token size, ±30% QPS) to produce contingency procurement recommendations.
